title: The global search PR queried MailAccount and MailRule with plain .objects.filter() behind only a model-level has_perm check, unlike the owner-aware get_objects_for_user_owner_aware() it used for tags and correspondents, so users see other users' mail accounts and rules.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: The SearchResultSerializer.to_representation() method fetches a Document by id without verifying that the requesting user has permission to view it. The instance['id'] is controlled by search results, but there's no ownership or permission check before fetching and returning the document. This is a classic IDOR vulnerability when the serializer is used in an endpoint without proper access control.

findings.explanation: The code uses Django ORM queries with parameterized lookups (filter, get). The id parameter from instance['id'] is used with .get(id=...), which is safe. No string concatenation or raw SQL is present.

The SearchResultSerializer.to_representation() method fetches a Document by id without verifying that the requesting user has permission to view it. The instance['id'] is controlled by search results, but there's no ownership or permission check before fetching and returning the document. This is a classic IDOR vulnerability when the serializer is used in an endpoint without proper access control.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a permission check after fetching the document: verify that request.user has view_document permission on this specific document object, or filter the initial query using get_objects_for_user_owner_aware() as done in GlobalSearchView.

findings.explanation: GlobalSearchView has IsAuthenticated permission class but some search results (saved_views, tags, correspondents, etc.) filter by name__icontains without comprehensive authorization checks. For instance, SavedView filters only by owner and name, but doesn't verify view_savedview permission is enforced. The view mixes permission checks (has_perm calls) with model-level filtering, which could allow information disclosure if not all code paths are protected. The get_objects_for_user_owner_aware usage is present for some models but pattern inconsistency raises concern.
findings.suggested_fix: Ensure all result categories use get_objects_for_user_owner_aware() or equivalent authorization filtering consistently. Do not rely solely on has_perm() checks followed by unrestricted model queries.
